scenario: An insurance company's claims database only records claims above the $2,000 deductible â€” smaller claims are settled directly and not logged. An actuary uses the database to model the average claim size for reserve planning.

data.description: Only claims exceeding the $2,000 deductible appear in the database. Claim sizes assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $1,500.

question: The claims database shows a mean claim of $3,200. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean claim size Î¼ across ALL claims (including those below the deductible), and (b) the fraction of all claims that exceed the deductible and appear in the database.
naive_answer: The true mean claim is approximately $3,200 since that is the database average.
naive_trap: All claims below $2,000 are excluded. The true mean is close to the deductible threshold â€” about half of all claims are below it and invisible to the actuary. Using $3,200 as the reserve basis would overstate expected costs for the full book by about $1,200 per claim.

from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(2000-mu)/1500; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+1500*norm.pdf(a)/sf-3200 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,100,3199)
assert abs(mu-2009)<25
assert abs(norm.sf((2000-mu)/1500)-0.5023)<0.01
